strengths: A thread's words never sit in the document: every thread card is a private card (messenger.mjs:284-316, COMM-03), and a card whose place in a thread is the secret is veiled (messenger.mjs:23-42), so a player's console reads no other player's conversation.

Read means seen: a thread is marked read only while its window is drawn, on Chat, frontmost and the page visible (messenger-app.mjs:446-460), and the read stamp is the newest message's own timestamp, not this browser's clock (messenger.mjs:203-206).
A failed send keeps what was typed and says what is known of it - may have gone out, said already, or not sent (messenger-app.mjs:396-427).

One ruling per card across every GM and every copy of the card: claimCard on the primary, the buttons of a card held while one press runs, a refused second press told on a card of its own (messenger-app.mjs:740-786, bridge-asks.mjs:1324-1346).

The notice history draws a kept card only through two cleanings and importNode into a template's inert document, with its own tag, attribute and class allowlist (notice-history.mjs:166-420); the store keeps every account's section of a shared browser apart and never trims another account's section of this world (notice-history.mjs:683-711).
A notice never times out: a card that does not fit waits parked behind a count, and the newest is always shown (popup.mjs:67-72, 352-389).

The arrival notices are chained per owner, so the paid crossing's hook and the settled crossing that follows it tell a stash or a bedroom once (stash-reach.mjs:611-622, doors-gm.mjs:395-402; tier 2 A113-C4-3 and A113-C5-1b, results not read).

findings.title: A ruling card's buttons act on whatever character and item their data names: a card a player's console writes can make a GM's press charge a classmate Sanity or use up a classmate's item
findings.where: scripts/messenger-app.mjs:724-786 (wireCallActions wires any [data-drpg-call] button for a GM), 1211-1233 (ruleObserveMiss: chargeObserveMiss on data.by), 938-962 (itemNoEffect and itemRefuse on data.by and data.item), 894-899 (rulingThread sends the line to data.by's owner), 1429-1435 (cubGiveHope reads data.n); scripts/gm-bridge.mjs:143-161 (since F118 every chat-log card holding such a button is wired, not only one carrying callCard); scripts/call-gm.mjs:1077-1104 (the claim checks only whether the card was ruled or settled)
findings.what_happens: The legitimate ruling cards are written on the roller's own browser (use-items.mjs:595-610 promptAndCallGm; action-pipeline.mjs:1091-1097 missAction carries data.by = the roller's actor), so their buttons' data-* must survive the cleaning of a player's words, and scenario 30 checks that they do (30-security.mjs:748-773). On a GM, buildBubble wires every [data-drpg-call] button of a thread card, and since F118 the chat log wires every card whose drawn copy holds one. The rule a button names then runs on the GM with the button's data as its arguments: observeMiss writes OBSERVE_FAIL_STRESS onto game.actors.get(data.by) through the GM's trustedWrite; itemNoEffect consumes data.item of data.by through grantItemEffect; itemRefuse, reply, searchMiss and observeMiss post the GM's ruling into the thread of data.by's owner (rulingThread falls back to ownerOf when the card's thread player does not own the actor). Nothing on this road compares data.by with the card's writer (cardWriter) or the thread's player, and claimOnPrimary asks only whether the card was ruled. A Give 1 / Give 2 button's amount is data.n, read with no upper bound here (monocub.mjs:1551: wholeNumber with min 0 only); what convertDespairToHope caps was not traced.
findings.failure_scenario: A player's console posts into their own thread a copy of an Observe card naming a classmate's character with its 'Nothing was there' button; a GM presses it: the classmate takes 1 Sanity and reads '<GM> rules: Nothing was there.' in their own thread for an Observe they never made.
findings.expected: A ruling acts only on a character the card's writer owns (cardWriter and data.by, the check refundOnCard's own note implies when it says the card's data is the player's to rewrite), or on a card whose ask the primary holds (the rid road the Hope Call, Dynamic and trait cards already take).
findings.refutation_tried: Looked for a guard on each road: wireCallActions checks settled and isGM only (730-738); claimCard/claimOnPrimary check claim, ruled and settled state only (bridge-asks.mjs:1324-1346, call-gm.mjs:1077-1104); chargeObserveMiss checks the GMs' marks and maximum, not who asked (observe.mjs:927-942); ruleCreativeUse checks the item is still usable and the holder alive, not whose card it is (use-items.mjs:1016-1043). The cleaning does not take the buttons off: scenario 30 asserts that a player's card's button and data attributes survive it (results not read). The Hope Call, Dynamic and trait rulings are not open this way: they go by the primary, which keeps a yes only for the ask held on that card (messenger-app.mjs:851-887, 901-933). The refund of decline and declineMurder on the writer's own character is believed by design (refundOnCard's note, 1235-1270; listed under by_decision), so it is not part of this finding. What stays: the GM's press is needed and the button's label is the card writer's.
findings.tests_near: Scenario 30-security 'XSS: the card's button and data attributes survive the cleaning' (30-security.mjs:772) holds the half that must stay; no test or scenario found that presses a card naming a character its writer does not own (git grep of data-drpg-call in scripts/tests*.mjs and audit/harness/scenarios read for that case).

findings.title: The messenger's read map is one value for every login on a browser: a GM who reads a player's thread there marks it read for that player's own login on the same browser, and back
findings.where: scripts/settings.mjs:2106-2114 (messengerLastRead, scope client, a plain object); scripts/messenger.mjs:181-209 (readMap, lastReadAt, markThreadRead: keyed by the thread's player id alone); scripts/messenger.mjs:147 (unread is read against that stamp)
findings.what_happens: A client setting is one localStorage item per key for the whole browser - the module's own notice history reads it as `${MODULE_ID}.${key}` (notice-history.mjs:1162) and keys its value by world and user for that reason (notice-history.mjs:13-18), as the private cards' store keeps an owner per entry (secret.mjs:647-658, S11-29: 'one browser, two logins'). The read map is { <player user id>: <stamp> } with no world and no reader in it: on a GM's login it holds the GM's reading of each player's thread; on that player's login on the same browser threadStatsOf reads the same entry as the player's own. So a GM who read Aiko's thread up to a reply leaves Aiko's login on that browser with the reply already read (no badge, no count), and Aiko reading her thread there clears the GM's badge for it.
findings.failure_scenario: A GM checks a player's view by logging in as that player on the GM's own browser: the GM's ruling, read in the GM's session, shows no unread badge on the player's launcher, so the GM concludes the badge does not light for a ruling.
findings.expected: The read state keyed by world and reader as well as by thread (the notice history's `<world>.<user>` sections), so one login's reading is never another's.
findings.refutation_tried: Looked for a world or user key in readMap and markThreadRead: none (messenger.mjs:181-209). Two players sharing a browser do not collide (each thread's key is its own player's id); the collision is between a GM and a player of the same thread on one browser, so the severity is held to minor. That a client setting is one item per browser on v14 is the notice history's assumption as well (notice-history.mjs:1162-1166) and not read at a table here.

findings.title: Closing the notice history marks every unread notice read, the ones its filter or search hid and the ones waiting behind 'Show new notices' included
findings.where: scripts/notice-history-app.mjs:310-318 (_onClose -> markNoticesRead); scripts/notice-history.mjs:1123-1135 (markRead walks every entry); notice-history-app.mjs:363-378 (new entries wait behind the pill)
findings.what_happens: The window's comment says closing 'reads what it listed (P10-3)'. markNoticesRead takes no list: the engine moves every entry of this login whose state is unread to read. A reader who filtered the list to one source, searched it, or had new entries arrive while scrolled (they wait behind the pill, undrawn) closes the window and the corner button's count drops to zero for notices that were never on the list.
findings.failure_scenario: A GM opens the history, presses the 'Players' filter to find one card and closes the window: the six unread rulings and refusals the filter hid are marked read, and the corner button no longer says they are there.
findings.expected: What the comment says: closing reads the entries the list drew (this.drawn under the filter and search in force), and 'Mark all as read' stays the way to read everything.
findings.refutation_tried: Looked for a narrower call: markNoticesRead is the engine's markRead with no argument (notice-history.mjs:1188), and _onClose passes none. The design paper P10-3 itself was not found in the repository (git grep P10-3 finds only this comment and a tier-1 note at tests-tier1.mjs:14588), so whether the design meant 'all' cannot be settled from the papers; the comment's own words are 'what it listed'.

findings.title: The messenger's launcher is torn down and built again on every thread event, and each build walks every chat message
findings.where: scripts/messenger-app.mjs:41-51 (five hooks call renderLauncher), 1499-1536 (remove, create, append); scripts/secret.mjs:829-831 and 924 (every words arrival of a thread card raises drpgMessengerEdited); scripts/messenger.mjs:166-173 (one threadStats pass a task)
findings.what_happens: renderLauncher removes #drpg-messenger-launcher and appends a new button on canvasReady, on every thread message, on every read stamp, on every edited card and on every deletion. Every private thread card's words landing raise drpgMessengerEdited (secret.mjs remember), so a browser given the words of many cards after a return (askForWords answers card by card, secret.mjs:1440-1513) rebuilds the launcher once per card, each time with a threadStats pass over game.messages (the memo lives one microtask). A keyboard user whose focus is on the launcher loses it to the page whenever a message arrives, and a hover tooltip on it goes with the node.
findings.failure_scenario: A GM who reconnects to a season-long world gets the words of a hundred thread cards back: the launcher is rebuilt a hundred times, each over every message of the log, and a GM tabbing to the launcher with the keyboard during play finds focus thrown back to the page by the next message.
findings.expected: The button made once and its badge and name updated in place (as popup.mjs showUnread updates the notice button's attributes only when they change, 167-183).
findings.refutation_tried: Checked whether the pass is shared: a launcher and a roster built in one task share it (messenger.mjs:154-173), but each remember is its own task. Not measured: the cost per pass at a season's message count; scenario 86 counts messenger.threadStats (perf-counters.mjs) for one move and one write, not a return.

findings.title: gmPopup on a plain card's document interrupts a GM whoever wrote it, beside popupForce and popupCentre, which only a GM's card may ask - and a player's public card already reaches every GM
findings.what_happens: E02 (S11-27) limited popupForce and later popupCentre to a GM's card, the comment saying a player's console 'put a card that looks like the module's own in the middle of every screen'. gmPopup is read with cardFlag, which answers the document's own flag first, so a plain (non-private) whisper to the GMs that a player's console writes with flags { drpgMessage, gmPopup } raises a card on every GM; the module itself never posts gmPopup on a plain document (call-gm.mjs:978-986 goes through whisperToGms, a private card, whose player meta loses gmPopup at secret.mjs:1488). And a player's public card with the module's marker is drawn on every screen, GMs included (1212-1215, 1257), so the guard closes a smaller door than its comment names.
findings.failure_scenario: A player's console whispers the GMs a plain card with the module's marker and gmPopup: it lands in the GM's notice tile under a title the player chose, as a ruling request would.
findings.expected: gmPopup held to a GM's card or to the private meta the module writes, as its two siblings are, and the comment saying that a public card reaches every screen by design.
findings.refutation_tried: Looked for a legitimate plain gmPopup card: every module post goes through privately/postSecret (utils.mjs:701-768), so gmPopup only reaches a document by a console write. The public road cannot be limited without breaking a player's own announcements, so this is a nit about the guard's reach and its comment.

not_established.what: Whether Foundry 14 stamps ChatMessage.timestamp on the server or keeps the creating browser's clock. It decides the open half of COMM-15: unread is the message's own timestamp against the newest read stamp (messenger.mjs:144-149, 201-206), and a bubble appended to an open window goes to the bottom (messenger-app.mjs:505-513) while a window built afresh sorts by timestamp (messenger.mjs:113-118), so a message from a browser whose clock runs behind arrives read and moves up the thread on the next open.
